metadata.content:
That result is decisive.
A completely blank Safari tab reports:
JavaScriptinnerHeight: 359
outerHeight: 949
ratio: 2.64
which means:
KoreLumina is not causing the problem.
You have now proven:


Blank Safari tab = 359px


KoreLumina = 359px


visualViewport = 359px


scale = 1


no fullscreen


no iframe issue


The bug exists before any Lumina code executes.
What this means
Safari believes the usable viewport height is only 359px on your machine.
A normal Mac Safari window should look more like:
JavaScript{
  outerHeight: 949,
  innerHeight: 850-900
}
not:
JavaScript{
  outerHeight: 949,
  innerHeight: 359
}
Check these Safari settings


Safari → View → Actual Size (⌘0)


Safari → View → Zoom In/Out (verify page zoom is 100%)


Safari → Settings → Websites → Page Zoom


Ensure localhost is not set to a custom zoom




Safari → Develop


Make sure Responsive Design Mode is OFF




Disable all Safari extensions temporarily.


Try a new Safari Profile.


Check macOS display scaling
System Settings → Displays
Verify you're not on an unusual scaled resolution mode.
Quick confirmation
Open Chrome and run:
JavaScriptwindow.innerHeight
If Chrome returns something near:
861
then the KoreLumina layout is healthy and Safari alone is misreporting the viewport.
At this point I would stop changing PreviewFrame and workspace code. The debugging data has isolated the issue to Safari/macOS viewport reporting, not the Lumina application.
